newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end sharply up.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed sharply higher on Monday, with nearby two months up the daily 400 yen limit, reflecting the yen's weakness against the dollar, traders said.
The newly listed January 1998 contract opened at 13,870 yen per tonne and closed at 13,900. Daily volume was 84,092 lots.

Active short-covering from individual investors hit all months from the opening, due to the weaker yen against the dollar, traders said. "Nearby months, particularly, gained today on active buying from local investors," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot December corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.66-1/2 per bushel at 0835 GMT, against $2.67-1/4 at Friday's close.
The spot January of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.05-3/4 at 0835 GMT, against $7.04-1/4 at Friday's close.
